145: **PART II - THE FORMER PROPHETS: FROM JOSHUA TO THE THRONE OF DAVID**
147: The road climbed gently, winding around the terraced slopes of the Judean hill country. Jesus pointed toward the eastern horizon and said:
148: "Look at those hills. East of these ridges, Joshua led our fathers across the Jordan Valley, inaugurating the conquest of the Promised Land. Know that all of that triumph was pointing toward something immeasurably greater."
152: "After Moses died, the Lord raised up Joshua to bring the work to its culmination—to lead the people into the Promised Land, into the rest that God had prepared for them. And observe his name with utmost care: *Yehoshua*—which means *'The LORD saves'*. It is the very same name that, in its shortened form, you speak every single day whenever you mention the name of... well, you know of whom we are speaking![EN_REF:20]
154: *"As I was with Moses, so I will be with you; I will never leave you nor forsake you."* [Jos 1:5]
155: "And Joshua fulfilled his calling—he conquered the land, apportioned the inheritance among the tribes, and settled Israel in their rest. Just as Moses was called the servant of the Lord (*'ebed Yahweh*), so Joshua received that very same title when he drew his final breath [Jos 24:29].
156: "Yet there was an extraordinary encounter you must never forget. On the eve of the fall of Jericho, Joshua looked up and saw a man standing before him with a drawn sword in his hand. Joshua went up to him and asked, *'Are you for us or for our enemies?'*. And the reply was striking:
157: *"'Neither,' he replied, 'but as commander of the army of the LORD I have now come.'... 'Take off your sandals, for the place where you are standing is holy.'"* [Jos 5:14-15]
158: "The very words spoken to Moses at the burning bush! That Commander of the heavenly host—who could he be, if not the Lord himself, appearing in visible form to lead the battle in person? The true Conqueror of Israel was not Joshua—it was the Lord of Hosts.[EN_REF:21]
159: "Joshua prefigured the Messiah in every way: in the name he bore, in the victory he secured, in the rest he provided, and in the title he inherited. Yet Joshua died, and the rest he gave was earthly and temporary. There had to come another Joshua—another *Yehoshua*—who would bestow upon the people of God true and everlasting rest."
160: **12. The Judges - The Cry for the Coming King (Judges 2, 17, 21)**
162: "Yet after Joshua and that entire generation had gathered to their fathers, there followed the darkest chapter in the history of Israel. The people abandoned the Lord, worshipped the idols of surrounding nations, and aroused the holy anger of God. What happened? The Lord gave Israel over into the hands of their enemies. In their misery the people cried out, and God, in sovereign mercy, raised up judges—temporary deliverers—to rescue them. But no sooner had the judge died than Israel returned to corruption, and the tragic cycle began anew.[EN_REF:22]
163: "A heartbreaking, unrelenting cycle: sin, oppression, weeping, deliverance, and renewed rebellion. And do you know why that spiral never ceased? The book of Judges itself provides the answer:
164: *"In those days Israel had no king; everyone did as they saw fit."* [Jdg 21:25]
165: "Understand: the message of Scripture is clear. Israel needed a king! Not a temporary ruler, not a mortal deliverer whose breath departs—but an enduring, righteous, faithful King who would shepherd the people forever in the ways of the Lord. But we will speak more of the promise of the Messiah in the era of the Kings in just a moment.[EN_REF:23]
166: "Even in that dark epoch, the Lord did not abandon his covenant people. The Angel of the Lord appeared—first to admonish Israel that he would never break his covenant [Jdg 2:1-5], and later to Manoah's wife, announcing the conception of a deliverer consecrated to God from birth, Samson [Jdg 13:1-5]. That Angel—the Mediator of the covenant—was the living pledge that Israel and the seed of promise would be preserved even in days of deepest apostasy.
167: "The judges, including Samson, were shadows of the Messiah: each was a deliverer raised up by God to rescue his people. Yet none could remain forever. In every generation, Israel cried out for a new savior. That deep longing—that desperate need—could be answered only by the Savior who would never die."
168: **13. Hannah's Song - The First Prophecy of the Anointed (1 Samuel 2:1-10)**
170: "Then, in the darkest hour of the priesthood—when Eli was old and his sons defiled the sanctuary—a barren woman named Hannah poured out her soul in tears before the Lord, pleading for a son. And the Lord heard her. Samuel was born, and Hannah sang a hymn of praise that stands as one of the most sublime messianic prophecies in all the Scriptures.
171: "Hannah was a humble woman, yet the Spirit of God clothed her as a prophetess. She sang of the God who humbles the proud and exalts the lowly, who kills and brings to life, who raises the poor from the dust to seat them with princes. And then, at the climax of her song, she looked down the corridor of the ages and proclaimed:
172: *"The LORD will judge the ends of the earth. He will give strength to his king and exalt the horn of his anointed."* [1 Sm 2:10]
173: "Give your closest attention to this title: *his Anointed*—in Hebrew, *Meshiho*—his Messiah! This is the very first time in all the Holy Scriptures that the word 'Messiah'—Anointed One—is used in a prophetic context to designate the coming Sovereign![EN_REF:24]
174: "Hannah was barren, and God gave her a son. Many centuries later, another humble woman, Mary, the mother of the Messiah, would sing: *'My soul glorifies the Lord... for the Mighty One has done great things for me'*. Hannah's hymn and Mary's Magnificat stand as two sacred mirrors—one looking forward in prophecy, the other celebrating its glorious fulfillment."[EN_REF:25]
175: **14. Samuel - Prophet, Priest, and Judge (1 Samuel 3, 7, 16)**
177: "Hannah's son—Samuel—grew up to become a singular figure in the history of Israel. He functioned simultaneously as prophet, priest, and judge. He is the only man in all Scripture who held all three sacred offices at once.[EN_REF:26]
178: "As a prophet, Samuel initiated the enduring prophetic succession following Moses with unanimous national recognition. All the people acknowledged it: *"And all Israel... recognized that Samuel was attested as a prophet of the LORD"* [1 Sm 3:20]. The word of God was once again revealed through his mouth.
179: "As a judge, Samuel governed Israel with spotless integrity, traveling year after year on a circuit from Bethel to Gilgal to Mizpah [1 Sm 7:15-17]. He was the last of the judges, the living bridge between the era of covenant deliverers and the dawn of the monarchy.
180: "As a priest, he ministered during the collapse of Eli's house, serving before the Lord from his boyhood and offering sacrifices on behalf of the people. Through him, God's promise to raise up a 'faithful priest' who would act according to his heart began to unfold. He built an altar at Ramah and offered sacrifices, continually interceding for Israel before God [1 Sm 7:17].
181: "And it was Samuel whom God commissioned to anoint the first two kings of Israel. In his person, all three callings converged, beautifully foreshadowing the One who would come as the supreme Prophet, the eternal High Priest, and the King of kings."[EN_REF:27]
182: **15. Saul - The Anointed Who Failed (1 Samuel 10, 13, 15)**
184: "When the people demanded an earthly ruler, clamoring, *'Appoint a king to lead us, such as all the other nations have'* [1 Sm 8:5-6], the Lord told Samuel: *'Listen to all that the people are saying to you; it is not you they have rejected, but they have rejected me as their king'* [1 Sm 8:7]. Granting their request in divine forbearance, God selected Saul—tall, handsome, and imposing. Samuel poured the flask of oil over his head and anointed him, saying:
185: *"Has not the LORD anointed you ruler over his inheritance?"* [1 Sm 10:1]
186: "Saul was Israel's first anointed king—the first *Mashiach*. He was endowed with royal dignity and given the word of the Lord to guide his path. Yet Saul failed. He presumptuously usurped the priestly office by offering burnt offerings without authorization [1 Sm 13:8-14], blatantly disobeyed the command to destroy Amalek [1 Sm 15:1-24], and succumbed to pride, jealous rage, and bitter stubbornness.[EN_REF:28]
187: "And Samuel declared to him with solemn finality:
188: *"You have rejected the word of the LORD, and the LORD has rejected you as king over Israel!"* [1 Sm 15:26]
189: "Consider this deeply: the very first anointed king of Israel was rejected by God. Saul showed the world everything a true Messiah must never be: disobedient, self-reliant, arrogant, and worldly. Yet Saul's failure did not derail God's sovereign plan; rather, it proved that no merely human king could ever fulfill the eternal messianic calling. There was need for a different kind of heart—a man after God's own heart."[EN_REF:29]
190: **16. David - The Shepherd Who Became King (1 Samuel 16; 2 Samuel 5; 2 Samuel 23:1-5)**
192: "While Saul still sat upon the throne, the Lord had already chosen his successor. He said to Samuel:
193: *"Fill your horn with oil and be on your way; I am sending you to Jesse of Bethlehem. I have chosen one of his sons to be king."* [1 Sm 16:1]
194: "And Samuel went. Jesse paraded his sons before him—seven fine, strong, impressive young men. Yet of none of them did the Lord say, *'This is the one'*. Until Samuel asked, *'Are these all the sons you have?'*. And Jesse replied that the youngest was still out in the fields, tending the sheep. They sent for him at once.
195: *"So Samuel took the horn of oil and anointed him in the presence of his brothers, and from that day on the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon David."* [1 Sm 16:13]
196: "The youngest! A shepherd boy! The one whom no one even thought to invite to the feast! Thus works the Lord—he does not look as man looks. *'The LORD does not look at the things people look at. People look at the outward appearance, but the LORD looks at the heart'* [1 Sm 16:7].[EN_REF:30]
197: "And David grew, defeated the giant Goliath in the Valley of Elah, fled from the jealous wrath of Saul, and endured years of hardship in the wilderness, yet he never raised his hand against the Lord's anointed. And when at last he was crowned king in Jerusalem over all Israel, he knew full well where his authority originated.
198: "Near the close of his earthly pilgrimage, David uttered his last words as a prophetic oracle:
199: *"The Spirit of the LORD spoke through me; his word was on my tongue. The God of Israel spoke, the Rock of Israel said to me: 'When one rules over people in righteousness, when he rules in the fear of God, he is like the light of morning at sunrise on a cloudless morning, like the brightness after rain that brings grass from the earth.'"* [2 Sm 23:2-4]
200: "And then David added with unshakeable faith:
201: *"If my house were not right with God, surely he would not have made with me an everlasting covenant, arranged and secured in every part."* [2 Sm 23:5]
202: "David recognized himself as *'the anointed of the God of Jacob'* (*meshîah 'elohê ya'aqob*) [2 Sm 23:1], and he prophesied that from his line would arise the righteous, God-fearing Sovereign whose blessing would be like the radiant morning sun and life-giving rain upon the earth. David was the first firm foundation, but the ultimate fulfillment—as we shall see—belonged to an everlasting glory."[EN_REF:31]
203: **17. The Covenant with David - An Eternal Throne (2 Samuel 7:12-16)**
205: "And now we come to the very heart of the history of the kings. When David desired to build a house for the Lord—a permanent temple for the ark of the covenant—the prophet Nathan brought him the word of the Most High. And what an astonishing word it was!
206: "The Lord said in essence: *'Would you build a house for me? NO—I will build a house for you!'*. Yet the 'house' God promised was not framed with stone and cedar; it was an everlasting dynasty, an eternal royal line:
207: *"When your days are over and you rest with your ancestors, I will raise up your offspring to succeed you, your own flesh and blood, and I will establish his kingdom. He is the one who will build a house for my Name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever. I will be his father, and he will be my son."* [2 Sm 7:12-14][EN_REF:32]
209: *"Your house and your kingdom will endure forever before me; your throne will be established forever."* [2 Sm 7:16]
210: "Three times the words *'forever'* ring out! And God swears a unique, intimate bond: *'I will be his father, and he will be my son'*. Not mere legal adoption, but a relationship of divine sonship.[EN_REF:33]
211: "Friends, Solomon built the earthly temple, yet Solomon fell into sin and died. The kingdom fractured. The kings of Judah, one after another, faltered and failed. The Temple was burned to ashes by Babylon, and the throne of David seemed lost to history. Yet the Word of God never returns void! The promise of an eternal kingdom can be fulfilled only by a King who neither sins nor dies—the true Son of God in the fullest sense.
212: "And David grasped this truth with awe. When he received this promise, he sat before the Lord in worship and prayed:
213: *"Who am I, Sovereign LORD, and what is my family, that you have brought me this far? And as if this were not enough in your sight, Sovereign LORD, you have also spoken about the future of the house of your servant."* [2 Sm 7:18-19]
214: "Far into the distant future—David knew this promise looked far beyond Solomon, far beyond any mortal king. That covenant would span the centuries until reaching its final fulfillment in the Offspring of David who would be, at the same time, the Son of God."[EN_REF:34]
